assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. The work changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade exposure and labour-market adjustment. It combines the task-based framework with credible quasi-experimental evidence on local labour-market effects of import competition. It has also reshaped the policy debate on distributional consequences of globalisation.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task and polarisation literature and the trade-shock work. Hanson is central to the trade-shock and local labour-market evidence. Dorn and Katz made important contributions that cannot all fit within three names. Autor and Hanson capture the core credit most cleanly.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The key papers are about 10 to 20 years old and have been replicated and extended across countries. The scholarly debate has refined the findings rather than overturned them.
uncertainties: Credit for the task-based framework is shared with Katz, Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu, and the Committee may prefer a different grouping.
Magnitudes of the China-shock effects are debated, and identification relies on instruments and shift-share designs with known inference issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. Population administrative data were used to measure intergenerational mobility and neighbourhood effects at scale. The work links credible causal designs (movers, Moving to Opportunity reanalysis) to policy-relevant measurement. It has had broad influence on public and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader of the programme. Hendren is the strongest co-author on causal neighbourhood effects and exposure-based identification. Friedman and Katz are important collaborators but less central to the core contribution.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The main mobility and neighbourhood findings date from 2014 to 2022 and are widely cited. Long-run replication and external validity outside the US are still developing, and the laureates are relatively young.
uncertainties: Some neighbourhood-effect and mobility-measure results rest on specific designs whose robustness is still being assessed.
The Committee may think the field needs more time, or prefer to pair Chetty with a different set of co-authors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Estimating demand and supply in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices and heterogeneous consumers is a foundational empirical tool. It underpins merger analysis, antitrust and regulation and is used throughout industrial organisation, trade and public economics.
assessment.attribution: The BLP contribution is clearly identified (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes), with Pakes also central to dynamic industry models. Bresnahan has strong claims on earlier foundations of empirical industrial organisation but sits outside a three-person grouping.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The methods have been standard for about 30 years and have been widely applied and validated.
uncertainties: Attribution among Bresnahan, Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes is delicate under the three-laureate limit.
Identification of structural demand rests on strong functional-form and instrument assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 'Credit Cycles' model gave a tractable account of how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It became the workhorse for financial-friction macroeconomics and was highly influential after the 2008 crisis.
assessment.attribution: The core mechanism is clearly attributed to the Kiyotaki-Moore paper. Gertler and Gilchrist are important for the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand, but they sit in a distinct contribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Almost 30 years of use, plus the post-crisis literature, demonstrate durable influence.
uncertainties: The contribution is concentrated in essentially one seminal paper and its extensions.
Overlap with the earlier Bernanke recognition could shape how the Committee views the financial-frictions field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. They built a systematic political-economics framework linking electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal outcomes. They combine formal theory with empirical tests and created a field that has become central to economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest joint authors of the constitutional and electoral-rules programme. Besley is the leading figure on state capacity and accountability. The three-name grouping is coherent but leaves out other founders of political economy.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The key work dates from the 1990s to the 2010s and has led to a large, established field.
uncertainties: Some empirical results on electoral rules and constitutions are hard to identify causally.
Other political-economy pioneers could be competing claimants, and Persson's role on the Committee side requires disclosure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting transformed international trade theory and empirics. They brought micro-level evidence into models of the gains from trade, with substantial influence on trade policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution. Helpman's work on firm-level trade and on multinational organisation is broad and foundational. Redding has strong quantitative-spatial contributions, though he is less central to this core.
assessment.maturity: Mature. More than 20 years of follow-up literature and empirical validation exist.
uncertainties: Trade has recently been recognised (Krugman, 2008), so the Committee may weigh field balance.
Overlap with Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum raises attribution questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, microfounded and estimated, is the dominant paradigm in monetary policy analysis. It has shaped inflation targeting and central bank practice.
assessment.attribution: Woodford is the primary synthesiser of the microfounded theory of monetary policy. Gali and Gertler are central to the New Keynesian Phillips curve and to policy applications. Taylor, Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets all have valid claims, which makes attribution among many contributors very difficult.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The framework has been used for more than 25 years, though the post-2008 and post-2021 inflation experiences have prompted reassessment.
uncertainties: Crowded set of credible claimants and a limit of three names make attribution contested.
The empirical performance of the Phillips-curve core has been questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Moderately high. They provided theory and evidence on risk sharing, informal insurance, household decisions and market imperfections in village economies. The work links microeconomic theory to the study of poverty and has informed development policy.
assessment.attribution: Townsend is the pioneer on full-insurance tests and risk-sharing frameworks. Udry and Rosenzweig contributed key micro-empirical studies on credit, insurance and technology adoption. The three-name credit is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The central work dates from the 1990s and has been repeatedly replicated, although recent Nobel recognition of development economics (2019) could reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Development economics was recognised in 2019, and the Committee may judge the field already covered.
Rejection of full risk sharing in many settings complicates the theoretical claim.
